Process_Text.original: Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb powders, produced by EIGA with particle size ranging from 53–150 μm were supplied by the Institute of Metal Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences. New powders were labeled as R0.
Process_Text.simplified: EIGA-produced Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb virgin powder (53-150 μm), labeled R0 (0 recycling cycles).

Processing.Note: As-built, no heat treatment applied. Virgin powder characterization.

Structure_Text.original: Initially, the new powders consisted of γ and α/α₂ phases primarily, with the distinction between α and α₂ phases being challenging via XRD. The results by comparing the characteristic peaks showed that the initial powders were dominated by disordered α and γ phases. EIGA-produced powders exhibited high sphericity, with hollow and satellite particles being the primary defects in virgin powders. Powder particles exhibited a dendritic microstructure with dark solidification segregation (S-segregation) enriched in Al and bright β segregation enriched in Ti and Cr.
Structure_Text.simplified: Virgin powder: disordered α + γ phases, dendritic microstructure with Al-rich S-segregation and Ti/Cr-rich β segregation, high sphericity.

Structure.Note: Irregular powder fraction ~3% estimated from text describing initial powder characteristics. Sub-50μm fines ~3% and oversized particles ~5% from text.

Process_Text.original: After exposure to high temperatures and cooled to RT, both the powders in the hoppers and the un-melted powders were processed in the powder recovery system (PRS). The resulting blended powders were sieved, mixed, stored, and reloaded. First recycled powders as R1.
Process_Text.simplified: 1st recycling cycle: powders exposed to EB-PBF thermal cycle (900-1150°C, ~20h), then recovered via PRS, sieved and mixed.

Structure_Text.original: In powders from R1 to R15, the α/α₂ phase gradually decreased with increasing recycling number, and the interdendritic γ-region expanded. A small amount of irregular particles were observed in R1.
Structure_Text.simplified: α/α₂ decreasing, γ expanding. Minimal irregular particles.

Process_Text.original: After 5 recycling cycles. Minimal Al loss (<0.5 at.%) occurred within 5 cycles.

Structure_Text.original: In powders from R1 to R15, the α/α₂ phase gradually decreased with increasing recycling number, and the interdendritic γ-region expanded. A small amount of irregular particles were observed in R5.
Structure_Text.simplified: α/α₂ decreasing, γ expanding. Minimal irregular particles.

Raw_Evidence_Span: After 15 cycles, the proportion of powders irradiated by EB exceeds 93%

Process_Text.original: After 15 recycling cycles. Oxygen uptake progressed at 22 ppm/cycle during initial 15 cycles. After 15 cycles, the proportion of powders irradiated by EB exceeds 93%. At R15, two distinct types of irregular particles emerged: (1) fused satellite particles adhering to larger counterparts, and (2) particles with partial surface melting traces without complete fusion.
Process_Text.simplified: 15 cycles, O uptake 22 ppm/cycle, >93% EB-irradiated powders. Two types of irregular particles emerge.

Structure_Text.original: In powders from R1 to R15, the α/α₂ phase gradually decreased with increasing recycling number, and the interdendritic γ-region expanded. At R15, two distinct types of irregular particles emerged: (1) fused satellite particles adhering to larger counterparts and (2) particles with partial surface melting traces. TEM characterization identified Cr-Ti Laves phases (10-20 nm at R15).
Structure_Text.simplified: α/α₂ decreasing, γ expanding. Cr-Ti Laves phases (10-20 nm). Two types of irregular particles.

Secondary_Phases.Note: Cr-Ti Laves phases identified by TEM at R15

Raw_Evidence_Span: After 30 cycles, more than 99.6% of the powders were irradiated with EB at least once

Measured_Composition.Note: Al content 46.81±0.7 at.% from Table 2; Al depletion escalated to 1.62-2 at.% after 30 cycles

Process_Text.original: After 30 recycling cycles. Oxygen uptake accelerated to 27.33 ppm/cycle in cycles 15-30. After 30 cycles, more than 99.6% of the powders were irradiated with EB at least once. Rod-shaped particles dominated in R30 irregular particles.
Process_Text.simplified: 30 cycles, O uptake 27.33 ppm/cycle (cycles 15-30), >99.6% EB-irradiated. Rod-shaped irregular particles.

Structure_Text.original: By R30, the powder was predominantly composed of the γ phase, with S-segregation disappeared due to the high diffusion rate of Al at temperatures of approximately 900-1150°C. The bright dendritic structure caused by β segregation transformed into a block-like morphology (α₂). Rod-shaped particles dominated in R30 irregular particles.
Structure_Text.simplified: Predominantly γ phase, β segregation transformed to blocky α₂, rod-shaped irregular particles, S-segregation disappeared.

Secondary_Phases.Distribution: block-like morphology transformed from β segregation

Raw_Evidence_Span: mixed with 10 kg of new powders (from the original batch). Following remixing (termed R30b)
Post-mixing, the new powders comprised approximately 30.3% of the mixture

Measured_Composition.Note: Al content 47.86±0.5 at.% from Table 2; mixed with 30.3% fresh powder

Process_Text.original: Before the 31st building, mixed with 10 kg of new powders (from the original batch). Following remixing (termed R30b), the 31st building process (S30b) was conducted. Post-mixing, the new powders comprised approximately 30.3% of the mixture.
Process_Text.simplified: After 30 cycles, 10 kg fresh powder added (30.3% of mixture), remixed as R30b.

Processing.Note: Powder remixed with 30.3% fresh powder after 30 cycles

Structure_Text.original: After adding new powders, three structures were observed. Some powder particles lost their dendritic structure completely, showing dispersed bright spots enriched with Cr, with decreased Ti and Al content.
Structure_Text.simplified: Mixed microstructure: fully transformed particles + Cr-rich bright spots + remnant dendritic structures.

Properties.Note: Table 2: O decreased from 1200 (R30) to 860 (R30b) after fresh powder addition

Raw_Evidence_Span: By the 45th cycle, this ratio was reduced to 2.4%

Measured_Composition.Note: Al content 47.12±0.6 at.% from Table 2; achieving 48.12 at.% Al in R45 but subsequent cycles exhibited renewed oxygen increase (28 ppm/cycle)

Process_Text.original: After 45 recycling cycles. By the 45th cycle, the fresh powder ratio was reduced to 2.4%. R45-R70 powders exhibited semi-molten agglomerates with elongated structures that evaded sieving despite exceeding nominal size thresholds. The proportion of R45-R70 irregular powder is all greater than 30%.
Process_Text.simplified: 45 cycles, fresh powder ratio reduced to 2.4%, >30% irregular particles, semi-molten agglomerates.

Structure_Text.original: R45-R70 powders exhibited semi-molten agglomerates with elongated structures that evaded sieving despite exceeding nominal size thresholds. The proportion of R45-R70 irregular powder is all greater than 30%.
Structure_Text.simplified: >30% irregular particles, semi-molten agglomerates, elongated structures.

Raw_Evidence_Span: decreased further to 0.04% by the 70th cycle
progressive Al depletion (48.43 → 46.31 at.%) and oxygen uptake (560 → 2000 ppm)

Measured_Composition.Note: Al content 46.31±3 at.% from Table 2; Al content spanning 42.12-49.52 at.% reflecting heterogeneous irradiation history

Process_Text.original: After 70 recycling cycles. Fresh powder ratio decreased to 0.04% by the 70th cycle. Extreme variations emerged at R70, with Al content spanning 42.12-49.52 at.%, reflecting heterogeneous irradiation and melting histories across particles. The proportion of R45-R70 irregular powder is all greater than 30%.
Process_Text.simplified: 70 cycles, fresh powder ratio 0.04%, >30% irregular particles, highly heterogeneous Al content (42.12-49.52 at.%).

Structure_Text.original: In R70 powders, irregularly shaped particles increased, along with powder particles containing aggregated bright spots. Microstructures of irregular powders were non-uniform due to varying Al loss, appearing as lamellar agglomerates (α₂+γ) in Al-poor areas. XPS demonstrated progressive transition from mixed TiO₂/Al₂O₃ to Al₂O₃-dominated (82.11%) surface oxides after 70 cycles. TEM revealed Cr-Ti Laves phases and Ti-Nb-Cr precipitates (R70). FIB-TEM identified Ti/O-rich regions at R70 particle edges despite lacking continuous oxide films.
Structure_Text.simplified: Al₂O₃-dominated surface oxide (82.11%), C14 Laves phase, Ti-Nb-Cr precipitates, non-uniform microstructure, α₂+γ lamellar in Al-poor regions.

Process_Text.original: The Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb parts were fabricated using EB-PBF equipment (Qbeam S200, Beijing Quick Beam Technology Co.) with a constant accelerating voltage of 60 kV. The layer thickness was 50 μm, and the powder-bed temperature ranged from 900 °C to 1150 °C during building. Materialise Magics (version 24.0) was used for slice processing and model creation. Dense building process: Substrate preheating temperature 1070°C, powder bed preheating temperature 900-1150°C, building temperature 900-1100°C, layer thickness 50 μm, scanning speed 1.8-2.3 m/s, mean beam current 5.40-8.60 mA, line offset 0.1 mm, energy density 1.80-2.24 J/mm².
Process_Text.simplified: EB-PBF using Qbeam S200, 60 kV, 50 μm layer, 900-1150°C powder bed, 900-1100°C build temp, 1.8-2.3 m/s scan speed, 5.4-8.6 mA beam current, 1.80-2.24 J/mm² energy density. Built from virgin powder (R0).

Structure_Text.original: XRD and SEM analyses of S0 revealed γ and α₂ phases in all samples. BSE analysis showed equiaxed γ grains, fine lamellar colonies (α₂+γ), and dispersed bright spots (β₀/B2) along lamellar colony boundaries. EBSD analysis revealed pronounced γ bands in S0. No stress concentration was observed near γ bands but numerous γ [110]70° twin boundaries were present. HAGB accounted for 94.8% of total grain boundaries. Twin boundary fraction γ [110]70° was 12.5%. TEM showed dual-phase structure of lamellar colonies (α₂+γ) and equiaxed γ grains, with cubic β₀/B2 phase between lamellar colonies and γ grain boundaries.
Structure_Text.simplified: γ + α₂ phases, equiaxed γ grains + lamellar colonies (α₂+γ), β₀/B2 precipitates at boundaries, pronounced γ bands with annealing twins, 94.8% HAGB, 12.5% twin boundaries.

Secondary_Phases.Distribution: between lamellar colonies and γ grain boundaries

Grain_Size.Note: Equiaxed γ grains and lamellar colonies

From text: 'reduced by 40%' and '60% reduction from 2.1%' implies S0 elongation was 2.1%

Structure_Text.original: S15 showed more pronounced lamellar clusters. No γ bands observed (distinct from S0, S5, S10). EBSD revealed grain size <10 μm. LAGB accounted for 7.40%. TEM showed dual-phase structure with precipitates predominantly of Ti and Cr without significant enrichment of Al and Nb elements, corresponding to C15 Laves phase (Cr₁.₉₃Ti₁.₀₇). Precipitates were dispersed around the boundaries and within the α₂ regions of the lamellar colonies.
